diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $n=n_1(x)+n_2(x)\mathrm{i} \in L^\infty(\Omega)$ represent the refractive index, $n_1(x)>0$, and $n_2(x)\geq 0$
Without loss of generality, suppose that $n^* = ess\sup_{\Omega} Re(n)$

issues.failure_explanation: For $1/\gamma>1$, $\mathrm{Re}\,a(\Psi,T\Psi)$ contains the cross term $2k^2\mathrm{Re}(n\varphi,\psi)$ (and, in Lemma 3.1, $2k^2\mathrm{Re}\,b_h^E(n\varphi_h,\psi_h)$). The stated $\varepsilon_2$-interval is consistent only with the Young bound $2k^2|\mathrm{Re}(n\varphi,\psi)|\le 2k^2 n^*\|\varphi\|\|\psi\|$ with $n^*=\mathrm{ess\,sup}\,\mathrm{Re}\,n$. This bound is false when $\mathrm{Im}\,n\neq0$: e.g. $n=1+4\mathrm{i}$ with $\psi=\mathrm{i}\varphi$ gives $\mathrm{Re}(n\varphi,\psi)=4\|\varphi\|^2>n^*\|\varphi\|^2$. The paper's scope includes absorbing media ($n=n_1+\mathrm{i}n_2$, $n_2\ge0$; Example 4 uses $n=2+4\mathrm{i}$), so the $1/\gamma>1$ proof is invalid as written, although the lemma's statement remains true with $K$ depending on $\|n\|_{L^\infty}$.

failure_location.quote: we can use the proof method of Lemma 3.1 in \cite{WangBiY2023} to obtain the desired conclusion by choosing $0 < \gamma < \varepsilon_1 < 1$ and $\frac{k^2 n^*}{K - \beta k^2} < \varepsilon_2 < \frac{K}{k^2 n^*} - 1$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In the case $1/\gamma>1$ of Lemmas 2.1 and 3.1, bound the cross terms $2k^2\mathrm{Re}(n\varphi,\psi)$ and $2k^2\mathrm{Re}\,b_h^E(n\varphi_h,\psi_h)$ using $\|n\|_{L^\infty}$ (rather than $n^*$) and choose $K$ accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The case $1/\gamma>1$ of the weak $\mathds{T}$-coercivity (continuous Lemma 2.1 and the 'similarly' case of discrete Lemma 3.1) is unproven for complex refractive indices; since the statements are true and the case $0<1/\gamma<1$ is proved in detail, no downstream conclusion is lost once the constants are repaired.
issues.title: Case 1/gamma>1 of Lemma 2.1 bounds complex-coefficient cross terms by sup Re(n)
issues.why_classification: The statements of Lemmas 2.1 and 3.1 are true; the repair only changes constants in the $1/\gamma>1$ estimates, with no loss of scope, rate, or conclusion.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Given \({\bf F}= (g,f) \in {\bf \mathds{W}}\), the discrete source problem associated with \eqref{a3.3} is to seek \({\bf U}^{\bf F}_h = (w^f_h,u^f_h) \in {\bf \mathds{V}}_h\) such that
S_b^E(\varphi_h,\psi_h) = \tau^E |E| \boldsymbol{\chi}(\varphi_h) \cdot \boldsymbol{\chi}(\psi_h)
For \(i = 1, \ldots, N_E\), the value of \(v_h\) at vertex \(E_i\)
c_0 b^E(v_h,v_h) \leq S_b^E(v_h,v_h) \leq c_1 b^E(v_h,v_h),~\forall v_h |_E \in \mathcal{W}^h_{l,E} ~\text{with} ~\Pi_{l,E}^{0} v_h = 0
\lesssim  \sum_{E \in \mathcal{T}_h} b^E(f-\Pi_{l,E}^{0}f,z_I-\Pi_{l,E}^{0}z_{I}) - S_b^E((I-\Pi_{l,E}^{0})f,(I-\Pi_{l,E}^{0})z_I)

issues.failure_explanation: Equation (3.5) (and similarly (3.12)) evaluates $b_h$ at data ${\bf F}\in{\bf \mathds{W}}=L^2\times L^2$: $b_h({\bf F},{\boldsymbol\Psi}_h)=\sum_E k^2[b^E(\Pi^0 f,\Pi^0\psi_h)+S_b^E((I-\Pi^0)f,(I-\Pi^0)\psi_h)]$. The stabilizing part is defined through the VEM degrees of freedom $\boldsymbol{\chi}(\cdot)$, which include vertex and edge point values that do not exist for $L^2$ functions; moreover, the assumed two-sided bounds on $S_b^E$ are stated only for VEM functions with $\Pi^0v_h=0$, so no bound of $S_b^E((I-\Pi^0)f,\cdot)$ in terms of $\|f-\Pi^0f\|_0$ is available. The final step of (3.18) and the $I'$ estimate in Lemma 3.4 rely on exactly such an unsupported bound. Consequently the discrete solution operators ${\bf \mathcal{A}}_h,{\bf \mathcal{A}}_h^*:{\bf \mathds{W}}\to{\bf \mathds{V}}_h$ and $T_h,T_h^*$ are not well defined on their advertised $L^2$ domain.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine the data term of (3.5)/(3.12) so that it is well defined on $L^2$ (e.g. drop the data stabilization and estimate the resulting $b_h$-$b$ discrepancy with (3.18)-type arguments, adjusting the eigenvalue-operator correspondence), or restrict the data class to $H^t$, $t>1$, and prove the required dof-stability bound for $S_b^E((I-\Pi^0)f,\cdot)$; the eigenvalue/eigenfunction theorems, whose data are $H^{1+s}$ eigenfunctions, survive.
issues.overall_effect: The discrete source problems (3.5)/(3.12), the operators ${\bf \mathcal{A}}_h,T_h,{\bf \mathcal{A}}_h^*,T_h^*$ claimed on ${\bf \mathds{W}}$, Lemmas 3.3-3.4 as stated for ${\bf F}\in{\bf \mathds{W}}$, the bounds (3.18) and $I'$ in their proofs, and the claims $\|T_h-T\|_{L^2\to L^2}\to0$ and $\|{\bf \mathcal{A}}_h-{\bf \mathcal{A}}\|_{{\bf \mathds{V}}\to{\bf \mathds{V}}}\to0$ are unreliable as written.
issues.title: Discrete source problems apply $b_h$ to $L^2$ data where the stabilization is undefined and unbounded
issues.why_classification: The construction is ill-defined on its advertised $L^2$ data class and the supporting bounds are unsupported; a supported repair requires redefining the data term or proving a new dof-stability estimate, with at most a limited weakening of the lemmas' data scope, while the main theorems remain intact.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: seek \(({\bf U}_h,k_h^2) \in {\bf \mathds{V}}_h \backslash \{ \bf 0\}  \times \mathds{R}\)

Since \(k^2\) is not an eigenvalue of \eqref{a2.9}, it is known that for sufficiently small \(h\), \(k_h^2\) is also not an eigenvalue of \eqref{a3.10} and $k_h^2$ converges to $k^2$ (see \cite{MengMei2022}).
by Fredholm's alternative we conclude that the problem \eqref{a3.5} is well-posed

issues.failure_explanation: In (3.10) the form $a_h(\cdot,\cdot)$ is built with the fixed wave number $k$; the sought parameter $k_h^2$ never enters the equation. Hence (3.10) as displayed is not an eigenvalue problem for $k_h^2$, the statement '$k_h^2$ is not an eigenvalue of (3.10)' is meaningless, and the discrete eigenvalue $k_h^2$ cannot 'converge to $k^2$' in this formulation. The Fredholm argument for the well-posedness of (3.5) rests on this ill-defined auxiliary problem; the actually needed statement — injectivity, uniform in $h$, of the fixed-$k$ discrete form $a_h$ on ${\bf \mathds{V}}_h$ — is never correctly formulated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reformulate (3.10) with the eigenvalue parameter entering the $n$-term of the discrete form (i.e. $a_{h,\kappa^2}$), replace the garbled sentence by 'for sufficiently small $h$, $k^2$ is not a discrete eigenvalue', and conclude well-posedness of (3.5) via the standard uniform inf-sup/compactness argument used in the continuous case.
issues.overall_effect: The justification of the well-posedness of the discrete source problem (3.5), and hence of the definition of the discrete solution operators, is unanchored as written (the conclusion itself is standard and true).
issues.title: Discrete auxiliary eigenproblem (3.10) is ill-defined and the well-posedness inference is garbled
issues.why_classification: The misdefined display and garbled inference have a unique, standard repair that leaves the well-posedness conclusion and all downstream results unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: for any \({\bf \widehat{G}} = (\hat{f},\hat{g}) \in {\bf \mathds{W}}\), find \({\boldsymbol \Phi}=(\phi,z) \in {\bf \mathds{V}}\) such that
where \(B({\bf \widehat{G}},{\boldsymbol \Psi})=\int_\Omega {\bf \widehat{G}}\cdot {\boldsymbol {\overline{\Psi}}}\)

Referring to the concluding remarks in \cite{WangBiY2023}, we have that for a given $f \in L^2(\Omega)$, ${\bf U}^{\bf F} =(w^f,u^f) \in H^{1+r}(\Omega) \times H^{1+r}(\Omega)$ with $\frac{1}{2} < r \leq 1 $

issues.failure_explanation: The duality argument needs $H^{1+r}$ regularity for the adjoint-type auxiliary problem $a({\boldsymbol\Psi},{\boldsymbol\Phi})=B(\widehat{{\bf G}},{\boldsymbol\Psi})$ whose data $\widehat{{\bf G}}=(\hat f,\hat g)$ enters both components ($B(\widehat{{\bf G}},{\boldsymbol\Psi})=\int\widehat{{\bf G}}\cdot\overline{{\boldsymbol\Psi}}$). The only regularity result invoked in the paper is imported 'for a given $f\in L^2(\Omega)$' for the primal source problem (2.8), whose right-hand side $b({\bf F},{\boldsymbol\Psi})=k^2(f,\psi)$ involves only the second component. No proof, citation, or hypothesis covers the asserted regularity for the adjoint problem with general two-component $L^2$ data, so the key estimate (3.17), $\|{\boldsymbol\Phi}-{\boldsymbol\Phi}_I\|_{{\bf \mathds{V}}}\lesssim h^r\|\widehat{{\bf G}}\|$, is unestablished for the dual problem actually used.

failure_location.quote: by Fredholm's alternative we know the above auxiliary problem has a unique solution \({\boldsymbol \Phi}\), and $$\|\phi\|_{1+r} + \|z\|_{1+r} \lesssim \|{\bf \widehat{G}}\|_{{\bf \mathds{W}}}~~(\frac{1}{2} < r \leq 1).$$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Establish the $H^{1+r}$ regularity (same $r$) for the adjoint transmission system with general $L^2\times L^2$ data via the elliptic-system regularity theory (the analogue of the imported primal result) and supply it where the auxiliary problem is introduced.
issues.overall_effect: The $L^2$-error estimate (3.16) and everything derived from it — the absorption step in Lemma 3.4's proof (which needs both components of $\|(\hat w_h,\hat u_h)\|_{0}$), (3.22), (3.27), (3.30) and (3.31) — rests on an unestablished regularity claim.
issues.title: Duality argument uses unsupported $H^{1+r}$ regularity for the adjoint problem with full $L^2\times L^2$ data
issues.why_classification: The missing regularity for the two-component adjoint system is a genuinely nontrivial contained argument of the type the paper itself imports rather than proves; all stated estimates survive once it is supplied.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed identity in Lemma 3.3's proof holds only if $a_h({ f U}^{\bf F}_{\pi},{\boldsymbol\Phi}_I-{ oldsymbol\Phi}_{\pi})=a({ f U}^{\bf F}_{\pi},{\boldsymbol\Phi}_I-{ oldsymbol\Phi}_{\pi})$, and Lemma 3.4's proof explicitly sets the analogous bracket $a_h((w^f_\pi,u^f_\pi),(\hat w_h,\hat w_h))-a((w^f_\pi,u^f_\pi),(\hat w_h,\hat w_h))$ to zero ('-0'). Consistency (3.6) covers only polynomial second arguments. For a polynomial first argument the gradient and $u$-parts do cancel by the defining orthogonality of $\Pi^\nabla$ and $\Pi^0$, but the $n$-term leaves $k^2\sum_E b^E(nw^f_\pi,(I-\Pi^0)(\cdot))$, which vanishes only if $n$ is constant on each element. The paper's own Lemma 3.2 quantifies exactly this defect for polynomial second arguments, so the claimed identities are false under the stated hypothesis of piecewise smooth non-constant $n$. issues.failure_explanation: This identity requires $(T_hf,f^*)_{0}=(f,T_h^*f^*)_{0}$, i.e. that $T_h^*$ be the exact $L^2$-adjoint of $T_h$. But $T_h^*$ is defined through the discrete adjoint problem (3.12) with the form $b_h$, so $k^2(u^f_h,f^*)$ and $k^2(f,u^{f^*}_h)$ differ precisely by the discrepancy $[b-b_h]({ f U}^{ f F}_h,(0,f^*))-[b-b_h]((0,f),{ f U}^{{ f F}^*}_h)$, which is generally nonzero (the stabilization $S_b^E$ does not equal $b^E$ on projection errors). The subsequent decomposition into $I+I\!I+I\!I\!I$ therefore does not represent the quantity being estimated; the unaccounted discrepancy is nevertheless of the same type and order as the term $I\!I$ that is estimated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the false adjoint-symmetry step by the exact identity, keeping the $[b-b_h]$-discrepancy terms and estimating them with the same argument already used for term $I\!I$ (they are $O(h^{1+r+2\min(l,s)})$), which again yields (3.23).
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the eigenvalue estimate (3.23), and through the smallness claim on $|\lambda_{j,h}-\lambda_j|$ also the proof of (3.31) in thm:added-1, is incomplete as written; the stated rate $h^{2\min(l,s)}$ itself is not contradicted.
issues.title: Proof of the eigenvalue estimate treats the $b_h$-adjoint operator as the exact $L^2$-adjoint
issues.why_classification: The leftover discrepancy is of exactly the type already estimated as term $I\!I$ in the same proof; adding and bounding it is a short local repair with no change to the result.
